svg.title: Baking a normal map: detail from a dense mesh onto a simple one
svg.desc: For every pixel of the simple mesh's UV map, a ray goes from just outside the surface inwards until it meets the dense mesh, found fast with a bounding box tree. The dense surface's normal is turned into the simple surface's own frame and written into the pixel. The picture is stored as a texture file, used as the material's normal map, and exported in the GLB.
svg.text: Bake detail (texture baking, first slice)
The simple mesh gets the look of the dense one as a normal map: bumps painted by light direction, not by geometry.
1. Pick and prepare
Choose the dense object. Its points
are brought into the simple mesh's
own space (as it is shown now).
A BVH (tree of boxes) is built so
a ray tests only a few triangles.
2. A ray for every pixel
Each pixel of the UV map is a spot
on a triangle. The ray starts a cage
distance above it along the smooth
normal and looks inwards. No hit:
the pixel stays flat (128, 128, 255).
3. Write the normal
The dense surface's smooth normal is
turned into the pixel's tangent frame
(along u, along v, out) and stored
as red, green, blue. Edges are then
spread 4 pixels so seams stay clean.
4. Store and show
PNG, SHA-256 as its id, a "texture" asset,
material.normalMap = id: one undo step.
three.js draws it as bumps; the GLB export
writes it as the normal texture. Done in slices
of 20 000 pixels, with a progress bar and Cancel.
